result.summary:
Rendering lead, round 3: the renderer is upgraded on every tier, stays within its 60 fps budgets, and I checked each feature in the post lab and in game (a demo match plus the Kael, Iska and Vorn ultimates). The game captures for the after shots were taken at 960x540 at high, mid and low, with before and after sheets for each tier. Everything is original, and from mid-way it follows the new binding MURIM.md art direction (ink-wash night).

What changed:
1. **Scene depth.** The HDR scene target now carries a depth texture on mid and high. three.js resolves it from the MSAA buffer on high; I checked that both formats are 24-bit, so the resolve copy works. Every frame also gets a half-res linear depth buffer in metres. Other modules can use `post.depthTexture` (current frame, for `onAfterScene` and later passes), `post.linearDepth`, `post.depthUniforms` and `post.DEPTH_GLSL` (helpers including `edSoftFade`). In-scene materials such as soft particles read the previous frame's linear depth, so they never sample the depth buffer they are drawing into; this works on mid and high without errors. `onAfterScene` and the env's puddle reflection still work.
2. **Ambient occlusion.** Half-res, with normals rebuilt from depth, a depth-aware blur and an edge-aware upsample. High uses 10 samples and a 7-tap blur, mid uses 6 samples and a 5-tap blur, low has none. Bright pixels (emissive surfaces and VFX) are never darkened. It grounds the feet and darkens armour creases and floor cracks without the dark blobs an earlier version put on the fighters.
3. **Atmosphere.**
   - Analytic height fog plus distance fog with a forward-scattering glow toward the sun, which follows `env.sunDir` (the eclipse) by default.
   - Glow from point lights in the fog, so braziers and VFX flashes light the mist; it is soft-limited so a burst of VFX lights never whites out the frame.
   - Light shafts from the eclipse corona at quarter res (two blur passes on high, one on mid).
   - The sky gets only 25 % of the fog, so the black sun stays black. Fog and shafts dim automatically when `env.setMood` darkens the world.
4. **Depth of field.** Off by default. `post.dof({ focus, aperture, range, near }, s)` takes a focus distance in metres or a point or object to track. It is a half-res bokeh gather with 32 taps on high and 16 on mid.
5. **Grading.** After ACES: lift/gamma/gain, luminance-neutral split toning, and presets `night` (default), `ink`, `eclipse`, `ember`, `frost`, `storm`, `victory`, `neutral`, all reachable through `post.grade` and `post.to`. `post.reset()` returns to `night`.
   - The flash and mono/invert features are kept. Following MURIM.md, the mono impact frame is now ink on paper (rough brush edge, paper fibre); an inverted frame swaps ink and paper instead of producing a photo negative. `fx.ink = 0` restores the old black-and-white look.
6. **Shadows.** A new manager, `ctx.shadows` (created in `app.js`), fits the key light's shadow frustum to the visible shadow casters every frame. Inside the render, after matrices update and before the shadow pass, it samples the skeletons' bones. The window is square, snapped to a world-fixed texel grid, steps through fixed sizes with a delay before shrinking, and sets bias in texels. High at 2048 goes from about 8.3 mm to 3–5 mm texels, mid at 1024 to about 4–9 mm. In close-ups I saw no acne and no peter-panning. The env keeps ownership of the light itself; the manager only touches the shadow camera's bounds, near/far and bias.
7. **Sharpening and dithering.** The composite sharpens automatically when dynamic resolution drops below 100 %, with no ringing (`fx.sharpen = -1` turns it off). A ±1-step dither removes banding in fog and dark gradients.

Quality tiers gained new knobs (`depth`, `ao`, `fog`, `shafts`, `dof`) and URL overrides for A/B checks (`#ao #fog #shafts #dof #msaa #shadow`). Every post shader compiles at startup and runtime switches are plain uniforms. The shader-program count is identical before and after an ultimate, and after turning on DOF, debug views, radial blur, chromatic aberration and impact frames.

The API is documented in the new `src/post/README.md`, the header of `src/post/index.js`, and a new "Post and quality" section in `CONTRACT.md` (I also updated its Core API table and the ownership line for `src/post`).
issues: GPU time cannot be measured under SwiftShader. Fill cost is estimated, not measured: about 1-1.5 ms extra on an integrated laptop GPU at high, about 0.6-0.9 ms on a mid phone at mid, low practically unchanged. Please confirm on real hardware with #fpsmeter; dynamic resolution (now with sharpening) remains the safety net.

Env team (optional): call post.setSun(env.sunDir, PALETTE.corona, 1) and post.fog({...}) or post.shafts({...}) explicitly per mood. The current defaults follow env.sunDir automatically. The texel snapping in env.setFocus is now redundant but harmless (ctx.shadows aligns the window to a world grid itself). The post fog stacks on top of the env's own shader fog; if the far ruins look too hazy, use post.fog({ haze, density, far }) rather than editing both. Note: the env.mood getter allocates on every call, so post reads env.uniforms.uMood instead.

Env team: the puddle pass in onAfterScene must never sample post.depthTexture while drawing into the scene target. On mid that is a feedback loop, because the depth texture is attached to the target being drawn into; use post.linearDepth or post.depthUniforms instead.

VFX team: soft particles and mist cards can spread post.depthUniforms into their uniforms and prepend post.DEPTH_GLSL to the shader, then use edSoftFade(softness). It reads the previous frame's half-res linear depth; on low it reads a 1x1 far texture, so the fade is always 1.

Camera team: drive post.dof({ focus: <head socket or fighter root>, aperture: 1, range: 0.4 }, 0.3) on close-ups and post.dof(null, 0.4) afterwards. post.grade('ink') suits cinematic intros under MURIM.md.

Game team: the fighter API helper in src/game/present.js exposes pulse, flash, impact, radial and chroma, but not grade or dof. A passthrough (h.post.grade, h.post.dof) would let choreographers use the ember / frost / storm grades in ultimates; post.reset() already restores the grade at round start.

Impact frames now render as ink on paper (fx.ink = 1, per MURIM.md). Inverted frames (feel.js KO/finisher, Iska present.js invert: 1) now show neutral ink on warm paper (about 0.8-0.9 brightness) instead of a photo negative. If the 'never a white frame' rule needs it, those call sites can drop invert, or set fx.ink = 0 for the old look.
CONTRACT.md still describes src/core as owned by the lead and FROZEN; I only changed the src/post ownership line and noted app.js and util.js in it. The director may want to adjust the core/ line.

Shadows: only meshes with castShadow should cast, because each caster widens the shadow window (fighters only today; the RPG boss later). Use ctx.shadows.rescan() after adding a new kind of caster mid-match, otherwise casters are re-scanned every 30 frames. Shadow filtering is three's PCFSoft; contact-hardening soft shadows were not added because they would cost about 50 % more shadow lookups on high.

Profiling JS numbers are noisy: about 5 agents share the 4-core machine and SwiftShader's GL synchronisation adds stalls. Post-chain JS was measured at about 0.3-0.5 ms (one 1.9 ms outlier with DOF on); the shadow fit costs 12-15 µs. Draw call and shader-program counts are exact.

The before sheets come from a build made at the start of this round. Character art, clips and materials changed in parallel, so differences between the before and after sheets in armour colour, poses, or Kael covering the eclipse in ult frame 1.90 come from other teams, not from post.

result.perf:
Measured with profile.mjs (120 fight + 300 ultimate frames, 640x360, SwiftShader) before → after:
- **High:** draw calls 43 → 50 (ultimate peak 61 → 68); post passes 12 → 19, +2 while DOF is on; shader programs 49 → 56.
- **Mid:** draw calls 39 → 45 (ultimate peak 55 → 61); post passes 10 → 16; programs 47 → 54.
- **Low:** draw calls 30 → 30; post passes 8 → 8; programs 46 → 46.
- Triangles are unchanged (one triangle per fullscreen pass).
- Program counts are identical before and after an ultimate and after turning on DOF, debug views, radial blur, chromatic aberration and impact frames, so nothing compiles mid-fight.
- JS: the post chain submits in about 0.3-0.5 ms on high (noisy on this shared machine); the shadow fit costs 12-15 µs per frame; no per-frame allocations. The per-module update timings are unaffected.
- Shadow resolution: high 2048 goes from about 8.3 mm to 2.2-4.9 mm per texel (window 4.5-10 m); mid 1024 to 4.4-9.7 mm.
- GPU fill (estimated, since SwiftShader cannot time the GPU):
  - Full-res composite: +1 depth sample, +3 samples (AO, shafts, DOF), plus about 150 operations for fog and four fog lights.
  - Half res: depth 4 samples; AO 14 samples plus a 14-sample blur.
  - Quarter res: shafts 1 + 2x16 samples.
  - Roughly 1-1.5 ms on an integrated laptop GPU at high and 0.6-0.9 ms on a mid phone at mid; low adds only grading arithmetic.
result.api:
ctx.post (full reference: src/post/README.md):
  fx numeric keys (pulse / to / setBaseline): bloom bloomThreshold bloomKnee bloomRadius exposure chroma radial(+radialCenter, radialAt(worldPos)) vignette grain saturation contrast flash(+flashColor) invert mono ink letterbox distortion ao fog shafts sharpen toneAmount toneBalance
  fx colour keys (to / setBaseline; THREE.Color | [r,g,b] linear | hex/css sRGB): tint lift gradeLift gradeGamma gradeGain toneShadows toneHighlights
  to(params, dur=0.3, ease) | pulse(key, amount, {attack, hold, release}) | flash(color, amount, opts) | impactFrame({duration, invert, mono}) | setBaseline(params) | reset(dur)
  grade('night'|'ink'|'eclipse'|'ember'|'frost'|'storm'|'victory'|'neutral' | {gradeLift, gradeGamma, gradeGain, toneShadows, toneHighlights, toneAmount, toneBalance, saturation?, contrast?}, dur=0.6, ease='inOutSine')
  setSun(dirTowardLight | worldPos, color?, strength=1, {point=false})   // until called: follows ctx.env.sunDir, colour (0.82,0.9,1.0)
  fog({density=0.018, falloff=0.6, haze=0.0012, maxOpacity=0.45, floorY=0, start=3, far=36, skyDistance=60, sky=0.25, color=[0.0045,0.0055,0.0085], sunPhase=0.8, sunScatter=0.006, lightScale=0.8, lightRadius=0.35, dim=0}, dur=0) -> live params
  fogLights([{pos, color, intensity (cd), radius}] | null)   // null = strongest visible scene PointLights (4 high / 2 mid)
  shafts({strength=0.9, threshold=0.25, radius=0.3, length=0.9, decay=0.965, glow=0, skyDepth=26}, dur=0) -> live params
  ao({radius=0.4, intensity=1.25, bias=0.002, fadeFar=40}) -> current values (null on tiers without AO); strength = fx.ao
  dof({focus: metres | Vector3 | [x,y,z] | Object3D | () => pos, aperture=1 (0..1.5), range=0.6 (m), near=1}, dur=0.35); dof(null, dur); dofActive
  depthTexture (THREE.DepthTexture, current frame, raw [0,1]; valid in onAfterScene and later; read the getter every frame) | linearDepth (half-res R16F metres, last frame)
  depthUniforms {tSceneDepth, uSceneRes, uCamNearFar, uCamProj} + DEPTH_GLSL: edSceneDepth(), edFragDepth(), edSoftFade(softness)   // in-scene ShaderMaterials: uniforms: { ...ctx.post.depthUniforms, ... }
  onAfterScene(fn(renderer, sceneTarget, camera)) -> off | distortionScene | debugView('ao'|'depth'|'shafts'|'dof'|'off') | features {depth, ao, fog, shafts, dof} | stats {passes, msPost (#prof)} | prewarm()
ctx.shadows (src/post/shadows.js): setKey(light|null) | mode = 'auto' | 'manual' | 'off' | focus(center: Vector3|[x,y,z], radius m) (switches to manual) | rescan() | params {margin, minExtent, maxExtent, step, shrinkDelay, biasTexels, normalBiasTexels, bonePad, depthPad} | info {mode, extent, texel, near, far, casters, fitted}
ctx.quality adds: depth, ao (0|1|2), fog (0|1|2), shafts (0|1|2), dof (0|1|2); URL overrides #ao #fog #shafts #dof #msaa #shadow
__ED.info() adds post {depth, ao, fog, shafts, dof, passes} and shadow {size, extent, texelMm, casters, fitted}
